summary: The subprime mortgage crisis was a multinational financial crisis between 2007 and 2010, triggered by the bursting of the U.S. housing bubble and high-risk mortgage lending. It led to a severe recession, massive job losses, and government bailouts, with long-lasting economic consequences.
entities: Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act

claims.text: The subprime mortgage crisis occurred between 2007 and 2010 and contributed to the 2008 financial crisis.
claims.evidence_quote: The American **subprime mortgage crisis** was a multinational [financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_crisis "Financial crisis") that occurred between 2007 and 2010, contributing to the [2008 financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis "2008 financial crisis").

claims.text: Nearly 9 million jobs were lost during 2008 and 2009, roughly 6% of the workforce.
claims.evidence_quote: The U.S. entered a deep recession, with nearly 9 million jobs lost during 2008 and 2009, roughly 6% of the workforce.

claims.text: U.S. household net worth declined by nearly $13 trillion (20%) from its Q2 2007 pre-crisis peak.
claims.evidence_quote: U.S. household net worth declined by nearly $13 [trillion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trillion_(short_scale) "Trillion (short scale)") (20%) from its Q2 2007 pre-crisis peak, recovering by Q4 2012.

claims.text: U.S. housing prices fell nearly 30% on average and the stock market fell approximately 50% by early 2009.
claims.evidence_quote: U.S. housing prices fell nearly 30% on average and the U.S. stock market fell approximately 50% by early 2009, with stocks regaining their December 2007 level during September 2012.

claims.text: One estimate of lost output and income from the crisis is at least 40% of 2007 GDP.
claims.evidence_quote: One estimate of lost output and income from the crisis comes to "at least 40% of 2007 [gross domestic product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product")".

claims.text: European banking impairments were estimated at €940 billion between 2008 and 2012.
claims.evidence_quote: Europe also continued to struggle with [its own economic crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_debt_crisis "European debt crisis"), with elevated unemployment and severe banking impairments estimated at €940 billion between 2008 and 2012.

claims.text: As of January 2021, the U.S. government had earned a $109 billion profit on bailout funds, considering interest.
claims.evidence_quote: The Treasury had earned another $323B in interest on bailout loans, resulting in a $109B profit as of January 2021.

claims.text: Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy in September 2008.
claims.evidence_quote: Most notably, [Lehman Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehman_Brothers "Lehman Brothers"), a major mortgage lender, [filed for bankruptcy in September 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bankruptcy_of_Lehman_Brothers "Bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers").

claims.text: The immediate cause of the crisis was the bursting of the United States housing bubble, which peaked in approximately 2006.
claims.evidence_quote: The immediate cause of the crisis was the bursting of the [United States housing bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_housing_bubble "United States housing bubble") which peaked in approximately 2006.

claims.text: Bear Stearns announced in July 2007 that two of its hedge funds had imploded, which was a proximate catalyst for the financial market disruption.
claims.evidence_quote: This became apparent by July 2007, when investment bank [Bear Stearns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear_Stearns "Bear Stearns") announced that two of its [hedge funds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedge_fund "Hedge fund") had imploded.

claims.text: Economist Mark Zandi wrote that the 2007 Bear Stearns event was "arguably the proximate catalyst" for the financial market disruption.
claims.evidence_quote: Economist [Mark Zandi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Zandi "Mark Zandi") wrote that this 2007 event was "arguably the proximate catalyst" for the financial market disruption that followed.

claims.text: Between January 1 and October 11, 2008, U.S. stock owners suffered about $8 trillion in losses, as holdings declined from $20 trillion to $12 trillion.
claims.evidence_quote: Between January 1 and October 11, 2008, owners of stocks in U.S. corporations suffered about $8 trillion in losses, as their holdings declined in value from $20 trillion to $12 trillion.

claims.text: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act was signed into law in July 2010 to address some causes of the crisis.
claims.evidence_quote: In the U.S., the [Dodd–Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodd%E2%80%93Frank_Wall_Street_Reform_and_Consumer_Protection_Act "Dodd–Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act") was signed into law in July 2010 to address some of the causes of the crisis.

claims.text: The Group of 20 leaders cited weak underwriting standards, unsound risk management, and opaque financial products as causes.
claims.evidence_quote: During a period of strong global growth, growing capital flows, and prolonged stability earlier this decade, market participants sought higher yields without an adequate appreciation of the risks and failed to exercise proper due diligence. At the same time, weak underwriting standards, unsound risk management practices, increasingly complex and opaque financial products, and consequent excessive leverage combined to create vulnerabilities in the system.

claims.text: Major investment banks had leverage ratios as high as 1:40, meaning for every dollar of equity they owed $40.
claims.evidence_quote: The ratio of their leverage ratios was alarmingly low, in some cases reaching 1:40. This meant that for every dollar of equity, these banks owed $40.
